identity.title: Solar Polar Brightening and Radius at 100 and 230 GHz Observed by ALMA

paper_type_evidence.quote: We analysed ALMA fast-scan single-dish maps described by (cite: White2017). The data were observed during the Science Verification period, 2015 December 16-20, and released in the beginning of 2017

question.value: Is polar brightening present in ALMA single-dish solar maps at 100 and 230 GHz, how large is it, and how does it (and the solar radius) compare with the FAL-C and SSC atmospheric models?

evidence.quote: Aiming to verify the presence of the polar brightening in the millimetric range, in this work we analysed ALMA single-dish maps observed at 100 and 230 GHz during the Science Verification period in December 2015.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00020.SV.

bands.value: Band 3 (84-116 GHz), six maps; Band 6 (211-275 GHz), three maps; reference 100 and 230 GHz

evidence.quote: The data comprise six maps obtained in Band 3 (84 –116 GHz) and other three in Band 6 (211 – 275 GHz).
these maps were obtained by a single dish antenna with 12 m of diameter
they present nominal spatial resolutions of 58” at 100 GHz and 25” at 230 GHz
The data were observed during the Science Verification period, 2015 December 16-20

what.value: Quiet-Sun brightness temperatures 7280±250 K (100 GHz) and 5900±190 K (230 GHz) for comparison

evidence.quote: in agreement with the values suggested by (cite: White2017) ($7280\pm250$ K)
suggested that the observations were best fitted by the average quiet Sun model C (FAL-C) proposed by (cite: FAL1993).

what.value: SSC atmospheric model with extended chromosphere

evidence.quote: The observed polar brightenings were also compared with atmospheric model SSC proposed by (cite: Selhorst2005a)
we combine the historical data compiled by (cite: Rozelot2015) and (cite: Menezes2017)

simulations_or_models_as_data.value: 1D FAL-C and SSC models expanded to 2D (50x50 km2 pixels), brightness computed every 100 km and convolved with 25" and 58" Gaussians

evidence.quote: Each matrix pixel represents an area of $\rm50\times 50~km^2$.

archive_products_used_as_is.value: Released SV fast-scan maps described by White et al. 2017 used

evidence.quote: We analysed ALMA fast-scan single-dish maps described by (cite: White2017).

smoothing.value: Band 6 maps convolved with a 54" (18 pixel) Gaussian to match 100 GHz resolution

evidence.quote: convolution of the Band 6 maps and a bi-dimensional gaussian beam with 54” (18 pixels)

what.value: Quiet Sun Tb taken as mean of 120"x120" area at disc center

evidence.quote: Following the method used by (cite: White2017), the $T_{qS}$ of each map was assumed to be the mean brightness temperature of a small area at disc center

what.value: Polar brightening from average of 61 radial profiles

evidence.quote: Following (cite: Selhorst2003; Selhorst2011), the polar brightening was estimated from the average of 61 radial profiles
Following (cite: Costa1999), the radius was determined at the point in which the brightness temperature drops to 50% of the $T_{qS}$ value.

evidence.quote: determined by the relation $\theta_{100}^2=\theta_{230}^2+\theta_x^2$, assuming that the ALMA observational beams are gaussian.

method.value: Average of 61 radial profiles every 1 deg at PA 60-120 (South) and 240-300 (North); peak relative to T_qS

evidence.quote: average of 61 radial profiles through the disc center, that were taken every 1$^\circ$ between 60 and 120$^\circ$, and between 240 and 300$^\circ$ position angles

method.value: Contour at 0.5 T_qS, 1440 points, circle fit

evidence.quote: solar limb position determined by `contour` procedure of IDL at the level equal to half of $T_{qS}$; c) 1440 points determined over the curve resulting from step b; d) a circumference fit adjusted to the points.

method.value: Compute Tb from FAL-C and SSC with H and H- free-free opacities, 2D expansion with R=696 Mm, Gaussian convolution to 25" and 58"

evidence.quote: the brightness temperature was computed every 100 km in the center-to-limb direction, and these results convolved with a Gaussian function with the same resolutions of the observed maps
the shape of the simulated center-to-limb profiles generally agrees with the observations when the uncertainties are considered.

findings_qualitative.value: South pole brighter than North in eight of nine maps, though differences are within the standard deviation

evidence.quote: with larger brightness intensities at the South pole in eight of the nine maps analyzed

claims.hypothesis: Polar brightening exists at 100 and 230 GHz
claims.experiment: Radial profiles of ALMA single-dish maps at polar position angles
claims.result: Mean polar brightening 5-6% at 100 GHz and 9% at 230 GHz
claims.finding: Polar intensity exceeds disk intensity at both frequencies (lower limits)

evidence.quote: We find that the average polar intensity is higher than the disk intensity at 100 and 230 GHz

claims.hypothesis: Atmospheric models reproduce observed limb brightening
claims.experiment: Compute FAL-C and SSC limb profiles convolved with ALMA beams
claims.result: Both give larger limb intensities than observed; SSC closer
claims.finding: SSC better but still overpredicts, possibly due to spicules

evidence.quote: Both models presented larger limb intensities than the averaged observed values.

limitations_admitted.value: Sidelobes not removed so polar brightening is a lower limit; poor resolution

evidence.quote: there should be non-zero sidelobes in a radio telescope beam. Therefore, the derived polar brightening should be a lower limit.

referee_caveats_inferred: Only nine maps at different times with varying T_qS

data_public_as_stated.value: SV data released publicly in early 2017

evidence.quote: released in the beginning of 2017

reproducibility.score_reason: Data public and method simple, but several settings unstated and models require external tables.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Public SV maps, simple profile analysis and numeric results.
